chapter: Willie Lynch, the Blue Rhythm Band and Teddy Hill
title: Willie Lynch's band at the Savoy and how it was founded
summary: Holmes recalls Willie Lynch of the Savoy Bearcats forming a band for the Savoy manager, with Holmes on alto, earning more than Chick Webb's band.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: We're now at the Savoy Ballroom, Willie Lynch's band...
And he later is to become Earl Jackson when Irving Mills takes him on. But he had a band...

He was out of the Savoy Bearcats band, which was one of the first bands...which was the first band to open the Savoy, you know. He was the drummer in the band. And I think that was Duncan Mayo's band. I think Duncan Mayo was the leader of that band. Well, that was in 1926, that the Savoy opened up -- he was the drummer in the band. And later on, hen they wanted a band in the Savoy, Buchanan, the manager of the Savoy, got in touch with Willie, and Willie got together some musicians for him, and founded Willie Lynch's band -- that's all I ever called it.
Well, that went with the job. But I can't recall who else was in the band. I know Chick Webb was on the other bandstand while we was workin' there. But we were getting more money than Chick.
And Chick was supposed to be such a big

favorite up there, but we were making more money than Chick was, and we were just a put-together band -- just get together, you know. But that was because we held out for more money. Willie wouldn't work in there under a certain amount.
